answer: Pay emission to an irregular pulse of work, not to headcount. Every identity must split a compact original problem the way one cracks a walnut, then set the opened kernel on a public ledge so peers can test it. The next beat cannot land in the same clock window as a cluster of look-alike accounts. A farm that mints keys and dumps near-duplicate answers in one burst is collapsed into a single identity and earns nothing. Only an unsynchronized cadence of inspectable work unlocks voting weight.
